messages:
jen: Thanks everyone for joining the all-hands. Leaving this thread open for follow-ups about release cadence, oncall, quality bars, and SLAs. I'll answer live and drop follow-ups after.

samir: Quick Q — are we moving to a fixed two-week release cadence or staying flexible? Also what's the freeze window look like?

jen: Short answer: flexible with a preferred two-week cadence. We won't force a hard freeze every cycle; instead teams should opt into a 'release window' for coordinated rollouts. When you choose a window, the default freeze is 24 hours before deploy unless you request an exception.

matt: What does "opt into a release window" mean in practice? Can we still do hotfixes outside windows?

jen: Yes — hotfixes are allowed and should follow the emergency rollout playbook (link: https://go/release-playbook). Hotfixes require a brief post-deploy blameless review. For normal features, opt-in windows get priority infra capacity and canary lanes.

elaine: On oncall — will rotation frequency change? I heard talk about moving to 2-week rotations.

lina: Tagging @jen — we prototyped 2-week rotations on infra last quarter. It helped burnout but made handoffs heavier.

jen: We're standardizing to 2-week primary rotations across eng teams, with on-call buddies for overlap (first 48h shadowing). Ops team will publish a new rota and handoff checklist by next Monday.

matt: For SLAs — do customers get different SLOs for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?

jen: Yes. Hosted: best-effort with published latency profiles; Dedicated: contractual SLA (uptime + latency tiers) per customer agreement; Private: depends on deployment (we provide playbooks and support tiers). Product will surface exact SLA tiers in the console next month.

samir: Quality bars — any change to code review / perf/infra tests before merging to main?

elaine: +1. Also curious about model rollout QA (we ship models frequently).

jen: Quality bars: no lowering. Mandatory checks: unit tests, linters, infra/infra-integration smoke in CI. Perf/regression budgets will be enforced for critical pipelines — see the 'quality gates' doc (internal link: https://go/quality-gates). Model rollouts require evals on the golden prompt set and a canary on traffic with automated regression alerts.

ops-bot: deployment scheduled: service-cache v2 -> canary at 1977654400 by infra-deploy

lina: Can we get an example of a release plan snippet we can copy?

jen: Sure — paste this in your PR template:
```
- Release window: YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD
- Canary duration: 1h
- Rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 100% (monitor p95 latency and error rate)
- Rollback criteria: p95 +20% OR error rate >0.5% for 15m
```

matt: Nice. Thanks! I'll update our team doc.

jen: I'll follow up with a short playbook + template. If you need immediate help, DM me or ping #eng-oncall.

samir: :thumbsup:

elaine: :wave: thanks!
